questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: It was crucial for me to an exchange in central europe, to explre the culture

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Compared to other faculties we did not get a lot of information at the science faculty before the introduction day, but after that things went smoothly.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: on the social part we were invited to a bigger erasmus whatsapp group with loads of events. Study wise we got the information we had been waiting on, on the day of introduction.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: it was not always easy figure out the system, but luckily the coordinators were super nice and helpfull.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: pretty easy there are several housing oppurtunities around prague for stidents

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: its more expensive, but there are also better facilities. you can actually get decent accommodation near the center fairly cheap.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: we had an introduction day where everything was taken care of, but we did not get any information up until then.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: the coordinators were very helpfull, either in person or via mail.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: very. most of the classes was very easy to get into.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: show up on the dates you have been told, and they will take care of you.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I had a lot of elective courses, and there was a large catalogue which i could choose from, both MA and BA courses were available.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: At UCPH i spent a lot of time on campus, where as in Prague i only spent 1-2 hours a day and the rest we had to read from home.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: you wanna explore the country while you are there which includes a lot of travel which can be a bit expensive

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: especially going out to eat were very affordable, prices in supermarkets were a bit cheaper than in Copenhagen but more or less the same. In general Prague was a fairly cheap city.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Erasmus club did a bunch of nice events and tours which was really nice! for sports and clubs at the university there were very few spots for exchange students, but apart from that there was plenty to do.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: erasmus club arranged plenty of social events and trips, there were several sports programs at the university also but the spots were mostly taken by czech students.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: definitely going on weekend trips around the czech republic was very nice.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Czech Republic has a lot of cozy small citys that are easily accessible from Pragaue. other than that there is some really nice national parks for instance Krokonose, and bohemian schwitzerland.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was not that hard i think, i came down there a couple of weeks before the exchange started, so i had a bit of time to adjust which was nice. Some other students took the czech language course, were they got an understanding of the culture and met some nice people, i think  would do that i if i had the chance.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: most of the classes you have are with other exchange students, but there are several of social event on the school with the local students during the stay which you can partake in.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: wasent that huge differences.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: first of all Prague is a very beautiful city with incredible architecture. other than that there was always markets to visit, and in general a lot of things going on in the streets.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Take advantage of the many social events that are being organized, its a very good place to meet new people. 
Go on trips around the Czech Republic and neighbor countrys. 
remember to go out and eat, the czech food is not that bad and really cheap.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: the youtube channel honest guides makes great videos on what to see in prague.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Meeting people form all around europe

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: learning Czech words....

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
